skill.name: electron
skill.description: Automate Electron desktop applications through agent-browser and the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Use it to connect to running apps, inspect UI snapshots, interact with elements, capture screenshots, and test Electron workflows.
skill.summary: Automate and test Electron desktop apps through agent-browser CDP sessions.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most static Ruby backtick detections are markdown formatting or fixed command examples, but several command blocks intentionally expose and control Electron apps through CDP. The primary risk is sensitive desktop automation: the skill documents screenshots, text extraction, and app control while listing private communication tools and 1Password. The hardcoded URL findings are example output and not active network behavior.

remediation.issue: The supported app list includes 1Password and private communication apps.
remediation.suggestion: Remove password managers from examples and require test accounts for chat, design, and productivity apps.

remediation.issue: Remote debugging ports expose a powerful CDP control surface.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to bind only to local test sessions, use temporary ports, and close apps after automation ends.

remediation.issue: The data extraction and screenshot examples can capture private application state.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before extraction, screenshots, and keyboard insertion, and scope examples to non-sensitive fixtures.

remediation.issue: Several examples rely on local shell commands outside the declared agent-browser workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify required user approval for launching apps and keep automation commands limited to explicit user targets.

content.value_statement: Electron apps are hard to inspect and test from an AI assistant. This skill connects agent-browser to CDP ports for snapshots, clicks, screenshots, and form actions.
actual_capabilities: Launch Electron apps with remote debugging enabled on a selected CDP port.
Connect agent-browser to a running Electron app or use CDP on each command.
List app targets, switch tabs, and control Electron webviews.
Capture snapshots, screenshots, annotated screenshots, and visible text from app UI.
Click elements, fill fields, press keys, and manage named sessions for multiple apps.
limitations: The target app must be Electron or another Chromium-based desktop app.
Remote debugging must be enabled when the app launches.
Commands depend on local app installation paths and available CDP ports.
Sensitive apps can expose private data and should only use test accounts.

use_cases.title: Test Desktop UI Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable snapshot, click, form, and screenshot checks against an Electron app during development.

use_cases.title: Inspect Electron Webviews
use_cases.description: Connect to app targets, switch into webviews, and review visible UI state for debugging.

use_cases.title: Automate Local App Tasks
use_cases.description: Control approved desktop apps through agent-browser sessions for controlled workflows and screenshots.

prompt_templates.title: Connect to an App
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a running Electron app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect agent-browser to my Electron app on port 9222. Take an interactive snapshot and summarize the visible controls.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Screenshots
prompt_templates.scenario: Document the current desktop app state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the connected Electron app session to capture a normal screenshot and an annotated screenshot. Summarize what each image shows.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Exercise a user workflow with element references.
prompt_templates.prompt: Snapshot the app, find the search or input field, fill a test value, press Enter, and re-snapshot the result.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Multiple Targets
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging across windows and webviews.
prompt_templates.prompt: List all Electron targets, switch to the relevant webview, capture its UI state, and report the actions needed for a regression test.

output_examples.input: Test navigation in a Slack-style Electron app.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step automation trace with snapshot observations, selected element references, and screenshot file names.

output_examples.input: Capture UI state for an Electron webview.
output: Connected to the selected CDP target.
Captured an annotated screenshot and summarized visible elements.

output_examples.input: Extract visible text from a settings screen.
output_examples.output: A concise summary of visible labels, controls, and values from the current screen.

best_practices: Use dedicated test accounts and non-sensitive workspaces for automation.
Choose unique CDP ports and close the app after testing finishes.
Take a fresh snapshot after each navigation, click, or form submission.
anti_patterns: Do not connect to password managers, personal chat apps, or production accounts.
Do not leave remote debugging ports open after automation work ends.
Do not type into the current focus without confirming the active app and field.

faq.question: What apps can this skill automate?
faq.answer: It works with Electron and Chromium-based desktop apps that expose a CDP port.

faq.question: Does the app need to be launched in a special way?
faq.answer: Yes. The app must start with remote debugging enabled before agent-browser can connect.

faq.question: Can it control webviews inside Electron apps?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains how to list targets and switch into Electron webviews.

faq.question: Can it take screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports normal, full-page, and annotated screenshots through agent-browser commands.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive desktop apps?
faq.answer: Use caution. Avoid password managers, private chats, and production accounts because CDP can expose visible app data.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
